entities.name: Ponç Hug IV, Count of Empúries
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ponç Hug IV, also known as Ponç V, Count of Empúries, reigned from 1277 until his death in 1313, marking a turbulent period for the small but strategically vital Catalan county. Son of Hug V and Sibila de Palau, Ponç Hug IV inherited a domain nestled precariously between the powerful Crown of Aragon and the ambitious Kingdom of France. His significance lies in his persistent, often defiant, assertion of autonomous comital power against the centralizing ambitions of the Aragonese monarchs, particularly Peter III and Alfonso III, transforming Empúries into a key flashpoint in late 13th-century Mediterranean geopolitics.

His tenure was defined by military engagement and diplomatic maneuvering. In 1285, during the Aragonese Crusade, Ponç Hug IV notably sided with Philip III of France against his own suzerain, Peter III of Aragon, a move that led to the French occupation of Empúries and his subsequent exile. He was only restored to his county after the Peace of Tarascon in 1291. Additionally, he briefly held the viscounty of Bas (1285-1291), expanding his influence, though this was ultimately lost. His campaigns extended beyond Catalonia, participating in Aragonese expeditions to Sardinia and the conquest of Menorca in 1287, demonstrating his complex loyalties and military prowess.

The legacy of Ponç Hug IV is one of both regional instability and a strong, if ultimately unsustainable, defense of feudal prerogatives against emergent state power. His actions contributed to the volatile border dynamics between France and Aragon, an area of constant contention for centuries. While his direct challenges to the Aragonese crown were ultimately contained, his reign underscored the persistent centrifugal forces within the Crown of Aragon and the difficulties faced by monarchs in consolidating authority over entrenched regional nobilities.

His actions influenced border dynamics between France and Aragon for decades.
